items: GitHub Actions extension (off by default; turn it on in Settings > Extensions): a toolbar button shows your pinned workflows in a panel under the tabs. See jobs and steps, re-run all or failed jobs, and get a red dot when a pinned run fails. On a GitHub workflow or run page in the built-in browser, click Add to Devkitty to pin it.

Settings: a new About page, a Shortcuts page with on/off checkboxes, a hotkey recorder popup and filters, list-style editors for pinned workflows and browser rules, and Settings JSON with Save, Save As and autocomplete with descriptions.
Terminal: an optional background image with opacity and fit; Warn Before Quit, tab close button options, scroll speed and an optional scroll bar. An app update never asks before it restarts.
Workspace: choose where new tabs and new workspaces open (Top, After current, Bottom / Left, After current, Right).
Browser: open http(s) terminal links in Devkitty, a list of hosts allowed over plain HTTP, Remove Website Data, more search engines, and an Open supported files in Devkitty switch.

Browser: Import Browser Sessions copies only sign-in cookies from Chrome-type browsers, Firefox or Safari, so you stay signed in. macOS may ask for your Keychain password or Full Disk Access (Safari). Not yet tested with every real browser profile.
Tab groups: opening a group slides its tabs out from under the group label; tabs sit closer together.
Notifications settings show whether macOS allows alerts, with a Send Test button. Reset All Settings keeps your privacy choices.

Less memory in the background: when you switch to another app, Devkitty takes focus away from its terminals, so the cursor timer stops and the graphics chip can rest. In a test, memory with Devkitty in the background dropped from about 370 MB to 135 MB; your numbers can differ.
Focus comes back to the same pane when you return to Devkitty.
Less memory for hidden terminals: when a terminal is hidden (another tab, a minimized window, Cmd-H or another Space), Devkitty frees its graphics memory. It is drawn again when you show it.
Less CPU: workspaces with split panes no longer re-measure their layout on every screen update. In a test, idle CPU dropped from about 39% to 24%; your numbers can differ.
Tab groups: Cmd+1…9 counts only the tabs you can see. Tabs inside a collapsed group are skipped. Previous/next tab (Cmd+Shift+[ / ]) still reaches tabs in a collapsed group and opens it.
Terminal: Command-click on any file opens the built-in preview (Markdown, text, images); folders open in Finder. A dot, comma or bracket after a path is ignored.
Downloads open in their own tab, without a Back to Page button.
Quieter when idle: fewer session saves and slower agent status checks while Devkitty is hidden. Claude Code no longer relaunches Devkitty every few seconds to report an unchanged status.
Bookmarks bar shows full names and scrolls sideways when they do not fit.

PR popover: GitHub-style comments (hidden HTML comments, collapsible details, alerts, task boxes, Show more), its own icon for each PR state, a robot icon and Autonomous badge for bot comments, and faster loading.
Browser back and forward buttons have a larger hit area. Open in External Browser closes the built-in tab.
Codex tabs no longer show the raw session ID as their name.
The mouse pointer hides while you type in the terminal.
Task Manager: see terminals and browser tabs with their usage, filter them, and jump to a tab.
Workspace tab groups like Chrome: colors, rename, collapse and close a group.
Attention: a moving border and an orange dot when an agent waits for you; blue dots for unread notifications. The progress bar hides while the border shows.
Terminal right-click menu. Every menu command is also in Command-P.
Terminal: Cmd-click relative file paths like clients/src/file.ts:5 (the file is checked first). Cmd-Shift-click opens files beside the terminal.
Bookmarks bar: right-click menu, glass edit panel, folders with site icons, drag and drop with a drop line, more padding.
Browser: one half-round tab shows and hides the URL bar. Downloads open in a new tab, so the page keeps its context.
Tabs restore at launch. Codex resume picker and Claude/Codex recovery fixes.
Tidier vertical tabs: selection, attention border, progress bar and title line up. New users start with an open sidebar and colored tabs.
Reduce repeated native layout measurement in terminal workspaces and sidebars, leaving more main-thread time for input.
Use Claude conversation titles, including /rename, while preserving names set manually in Devkitty. Place pinned-tab unread dots in the close-button position.
Show supported native Codex conversation titles, context readings and API-equivalent token-cost estimates. Add Copy Current Tab ID.
Add independent interface font preferences, roomier Settings and Command-P panels, compact About, and hover details for active tabs.
Keep disconnected persistent terminal tabs and recovery data. Include widget-fit, Claude subagent-progress and pull-request review-status improvements.
Restore the original compact tab fonts for horizontal workspaces and vertical sessions, while keeping larger text in settings and request panels.
Pull Requests now supports GitHub.com, GitLab.com and Bitbucket Cloud with separate native panels.
Bitbucket detects BITBUCKET_EMAIL and BITBUCKET_API_TOKEN from the environment or literal shell-profile exports. Settings shows Found/Missing and keeps the Create API token link.
Read Bitbucket mergeability checks to show verified Git conflicts. Bitbucket review and merge still open its website.
Restore cached pull request details immediately when returning to tabs; follow terminal folder changes and refresh in the background.
Fix GitHub check responses with empty links and recognize current Bitbucket SSH hosts and short commit hashes.
Improve text readability throughout settings and request panels.
Add an empty-tab bookmarks bar with favicons, folders and drag/drop sorting. Reveal hidden browser address bars from the top-edge control or Show URL Bar command.
Add Split browser right and Split browser below to Command-P's Terminal category.
Defer persistent-terminal attachment until its initial viewport is usable, preventing a reproduced tiny-layout blank-screen failure.
Improve terminal tab shortcut routing and Escape dismissal of release notes.
Preserve native Codex launch directories and remove forced remote-workspace routing.
Correctly show queued and running CI checks when GitHub returns an empty conclusion or a previous attempt's result after restarting.
Reuse the rotating GitHub CI ring for running checks, solid pending dots and neutral skipped icons. Keep completed failures visible.
Show reviewer avatars with GitHub-style status icons, using a bounded shared avatar cache.

Activate an existing browser tab and window when the exact same URL is opened from an internal link or another app. Preserve the retained page and split layout; different queries and fragments remain separate.
Preserve stale-session protections and existing browser-routing preferences.
GitHub pull requests now have a native glass panel with GitHub status colors, review details, checks, discussion and branch update controls.
The GitHub toolbar status appears when a matching PR is found, with a short entrance animation that respects Reduce Motion. Required reviews are shown as red merge blockers.
Keep the PR panel open for action confirmations; GitHub permissions and the current PR head are checked again before guarded actions.
Improve browser translation controls, remember the last translation language, and show the Devkitty cat on new tabs.
Carry forward workspace recovery, browser lifecycle, terminal link and widget fixes from recent previews.
Add configurable PostHog diagnostics and feature flags. Session Replay stays off.

Keep new terminal sessions running across app quits and reconnect to the same shell. Terminal settings include a default-on “Keep sessions running” switch. Closing a tab still ends its session; restarting the Mac ends running processes.
Preserve Codex Agents launches during recovery. If an ordinary saved conversation is confirmed unavailable, open Agents so you can choose it instead of guessing another conversation.
Preview Markdown and local HTML, find text with Command-F, and copy file paths from document headers and context menus. Local HTML scripts remain disabled.
Choose whether terminal links open in a new tab or split pane; Command-Shift-click uses the other action.
Use the macOS accent color in settings, consistent controls and shortcuts, and clearer extension names and ordering.
Improve Quick terminal settings, sizing, opacity and the fading screen backdrop. Add the “Use tab history” option in Workspace settings.
